svg.aria-label: Diagram: Bicep modules and loops and what they compile to, showing that modules become nested deployments in a single ARM template so each one carries a deployment name that can collide between concurrent deployments, that loops become the ARM copy element with a ceiling of 800 iterations, that batchSize creates a dependency between batches rather than a throttle, and the five loop forms with their limits
svg.title: Bicep is a compiler: a module becomes a nested deployment and a loop becomes a copy element, and both inherit the limits of what they compile to
svg.text: Bicep is a compiler, and its two headline features inherit the limits of their output.
Modules are converted into a single ARM template with nested templates. Loops become the copy element. Both facts have consequences.
module → nested deployment
A module is just another Bicep file — or an ARM JSON
template. It compiles to a deployment resource.
So it has a name. The name property is optional and
becomes the nested deployment’s name; omit it and a
GUID is generated.
A static name deployed concurrently to one scope can
show the wrong output. The linter now flags any
module that still sets one.
for → copy
A loop is the ARM copy element with a different
surface, so it carries copy’s constraints.
Values must be determinable at the start of the
deployment — nothing runtime decides the count.
Iterations cannot be negative or exceed 800,
against a template limit of 800 resources.
A resource cannot loop with nested child resources.
The five loop forms, and the question each one answers
[for i in range(0, n): ...]
I want this many instances
[for item in collection: ...]
one per element of an array
[for item in items(object): ...]
one per entry of a dictionary, via the items function
[for (item, i) in collection: ...]
one per element, and I need the index too
[for item in collection: if(cond) ...]
many instances, each deployed only when a condition holds
Every instance needs a unique name property, so the index or an array value has to reach the name.
batchSize is not a throttle. It is a dependency.
Resources in a loop deploy in parallel by default, and the order in which they are created is not guaranteed. There is no limit on
how many deploy in parallel other than the template’s own 800.
Adding @batchSize(n) creates a dependency on earlier instances, so one batch does not start until the previous completes.
@batchSize(1) is fully sequential. That is a rollout control for production updates, paid for in deployment time.
Where a module comes from, and what is allowed
'../storage.bicep'
local file, forward slashes only — the Windows backslash is not supported
'br/public:avm/res/...:0.18.0'
public registry — Azure Verified Modules, versioned by tag
'br:reg.azurecr.io/path:v1'
private registry
'ts:sub/rg/spec:2.0'
template spec
Registry hostnames are checked against a built-in allowlist — the azurecr domains, mcr.microsoft.com, mcr.azure.cn and ghcr.io.
A custom domain in front of a registry is blocked outright and returns BCP446, so vanity hostnames have to be reverted to native ones.
Sources: Bicep modules, iterative loops in Bicep, and template structure and syntax, on Microsoft Learn.
